_meta.description: Endogenous monthly world oil market for the world block: calibration of the prototype in scripts/oil_market_model.py. Flows in % of world consumption Q (103.1 mb/d, 2024); p = 100 ln(P/P*) real Brent; stocks in % of Q-months.
_meta.units_note: mb/d = million barrels per day; % of Q means percent of world consumption (1 mb/d = 0.97%); monthly frequency throughout
_meta.reproduce: python3 -I scripts/calibrate_oil_model.py --smm; python3 -I scripts/check_oil_model.py; python3 -I scripts/build_params.py (from this folder)

Brent_2025_usd.source: FRED MCOILBRENTEU, 2025; EIA STEO Oct 2026 Table 2

world_consumption_2024.source: EIA INTL 5-2 / STEO Oct 2026 Table 3a (103.10); Energy Institute 104.7 [unverified, definition differs]

opec_surplus_capacity_2024.source: EIA STEO Oct 2026 Table 3d (annual mean of monthly); 3.43 in 2025; ~0 from Mar 2026 (capacity trapped behind Hormuz)

stochastic_mean_offset.source: set by scripts/check_oil_model.py (K4): mean of the simulated monthly-average price above the zero-shock anchor; subtract when stochastic oil is on

w.unit: weight of end-of-month price in the monthly average
w.source: Working (1960): average of a random walk; implies AC1(d pbar)=0.25 and var ratio 2/3; matches 8.88/11.21=0.79 (Kilian T24 oil-specific h0/h1)

eta0.unit: |elasticity| of world demand to the crude price within the month
eta0.source: Hamilton 2009 Tables 1-2 (0.05-0.07); CCI 2019 Table 3 (0.017/0.031/0.080 IV); Kilian-Murphy 2014 / Kilian 2020 Table 4 (0.18-0.28 inventory-adjusted); BH 2019 (0.35 flow)

eta1.unit: additional slow elasticity, long run eta0+eta1
eta1.source: IRF calibration with prior 0.20+-0.08; LR crude elasticity = half of gasoline LR 0.58-0.90 (Dahl-Sterner 1991, Espey 1998, Graham-Glaister 2004, Brons 2008, Hausman-Newey 1995; BH 2019 s3.4)

rho_z.unit: monthly persistence of slow demand response (half-life 27 months)
rho_z.source: assumed; vehicle-stock turnover (BH 2019 s3.4: more than a decade); not identified by IRFs

beta_y.source: Hamilton 2009 Fig 2; BH 2019 prior 0.7, posterior 0.66 (replication); annual comovement 1992-2019 this report (advanced 1.07, EM 0.77)

rho_ylag.unit: oil demand follows the activity gap with this monthly persistence
rho_ylag.source: IRF calibration to Kilian (2009) SVAR bands, scripts/calibrate_oil_model.py step 1; REPORT section 7.5

eps_S.unit: within-month global supply elasticity (spare capacity use)
eps_S.source: Kilian-Murphy 2012 bound 0.0258; CCI 2019 Table 3 0.054-0.081 (Saudi 0.212, OPEC ex-Saudi 0.191, non-OPEC -0.004); BH 2019 0.15 [0.09,0.22]; Saudi 3-month price response 0.15 (this report)

theta_O.unit: monthly speed of output toward the target
theta_O.source: announced vs realised cuts 2022-24 (about 60% delivered); OPEC press releases

price_floor.source: cuts triggered at Brent $70-95 in 2022-24; fiscal breakevens Saudi $85-93 [secondary]; floor $71.5 in 2024 dollars, range $60-80

price_ceiling.source: ceiling $103 (range $90-110): shale breakeven $66 (Dallas Fed 2026) plus margin; weakly identified

kappa_L.unit: % of Q cut per month per 1% below the floor
kappa_L.source: Dec 2008 (-4.2 mb/d in 4 months), Apr 2020, 2016-18 decisions; judgemental

kappa_H.unit: % of Q added per month per 1% above the ceiling
kappa_H.source: 2021-22 unwinding 0.4 mb/d per month; capacity-limited; judgemental

tau_min.source: Apr 2020: 9.7 mb/d = 9.4% of Q (OPEC press release 12 Apr 2020)

tau_decay.unit: monthly erosion of past cuts while price above floor

market_share_unwind_rate.source: OPEC+ April-September 2025: 2.2 mb/d in six months (OPEC press releases 2025)

share_of_Q.source: EIA MER T03.01: US crude 13.27 mb/d / 103.1

eps_LR.unit: long-run elasticity of US crude output to price
eps_LR.source: Newell-Prest 2019 (0.32 at 1y, 0.95 at 5y implied); Bjornland-Nordvik-Rohrer 2021 (0.3-0.9 well level); this report LP 2009-19 0.19 at 12m, 2021-26 0.06; Dallas Fed Q2 2026

rho_stage.unit: monthly persistence of each of two lag stages
rho_stage.source: cumulative step response 0.06/0.14/0.28/0.37/0.43 at 6/12/24/36/60 months; EIA MER T05.02 wells drilled and T03.01 production LP

within_month_elasticity.source: Newell-Prest 2019 (-0.022 shale, 0.017 conventional per quarter); Kilian 2020

share_of_Q.source: non-OPEC+ non-US liquids excluding NGL/biofuel growth

eps_LR.source: Bornstein-Krusell-Rebelo 2023 Table 8 (0.20); Bjornland et al. Table A.6 (0.05-0.26); CCI non-OPEC -0.004 within month

psi.unit: % of Q per 1% expected price change
psi.source: IRF calibration to Kilian (2009) SVAR bands, scripts/calibrate_oil_model.py step 1; REPORT section 7.5; only psi*(1-rho_E) is identified

rho_E.unit: expected persistence of the price deviation

xi_builds.unit: stock-level feedback when stocks are above normal
xi_builds.source: stationarity of stocks; IRF loss flat up to 0.10 (scripts/calibrate_oil_model.py)

xi_draws.unit: stock-level feedback when stocks are below normal (scarcity premium)
xi_draws.source: stationarity; Sep 2026 Brent miss suggests convexity (REPORT section 9, item 7)

lambda_news.unit: loading of the news state on expected price

sigma.unit: % of Q per month, scale of the unit-variance innovation of the inventory/precautionary flow (the persistent consumption-demand part is theta_q times this)
sigma.source: IRF step 1 gives 1.613 for one Kilian sd (T19/T24 oil-specific impact 7.4/8.9% on the monthly-average price); times 1.10 from the step-3 moment match and hand adjustment (SMM 1.07); scripts/calibrate_oil_model.py, REPORT section 7.5

rho_I.unit: monthly persistence of the precautionary/inventory flow (at the upper bound of the search)
rho_I.source: IRF calibration to Kilian (2009) SVAR bands, scripts/calibrate_oil_model.py step 1; REPORT section 7.5

theta_q.unit: persistent consumption-demand innovation per unit of inventory innovation
theta_q.source: IRF calibration to Kilian (2009) SVAR bands, scripts/calibrate_oil_model.py step 1; REPORT section 7.5; BH 2019 oil consumption-demand vs inventory-demand shocks

rho_q.unit: monthly persistence of the consumption-demand shift
rho_q.source: fixed; carries the long-horizon tail of the Kilian oil-specific IRF (T19 h24 4.5, T24 3.0)

student_nu.source: handoff/second-researcher fits: oil-specific nu 10.4 (T19), 7.3 (T24); legacy oil_t_nu 4

intensity.source: CCI 2019 Table 2: 15 exogenous drops in 372 months (0.040); larger here to include sanctions and wars

mean_size.source: CCI 2019: average 1.9% of world output (Gulf War 7.6%); 2026 Gulf loss about 12%

rho_D.source: IRF calibration to Kilian (2009) SVAR bands, scripts/calibrate_oil_model.py step 1; REPORT section 7.5; Kilian production IRF keeps 58-64% of impact at h60

compensated.source: jump arrivals are compensated so the mean disruption is zero

sigma.source: typical monthly quota step 0.2-0.5 mb/d; judgemental

sigma.unit: % per month (prototype only; in the world block y comes from the bloc models)
sigma.source: variance share of aggregate demand 0.2-0.25 at 24 months (Kilian T24 0.19, T19 0.25)

rho_y.unit: monthly persistence of the activity gap seen by oil demand
rho_y.source: IRF calibration to Kilian (2009) SVAR bands, scripts/calibrate_oil_model.py step 1; REPORT section 7.5

cut_share.unit: announced OPEC+ cut as a share of the expectation shock
cut_share.source: Kanzig (2021) IRF calibration step 2: +10% price -> announced cut about 1.6% of Q (1.66 mb/d)

phase.unit: monthly persistence of the un-implemented announced cut
phase.source: Kanzig (2021) Fig 3 production IRF (-0.24 at h12, -0.53 at h24)

oil_import_share.unit: net crude imports / refinery crude input

crude_share_retail_gasoline.source: EIA, Factors affecting gasoline prices, 2025 ($3.10/gal); 51.7% average 2016-2025

gasoline_passthrough.source: FRED APU000074714 on MCOILWTICO 1990-2024 (this report); EIA Today in Energy 6850: 2.4 cents; 60% in month 0

longrun_elasticity_headline.source: geometric lag fitted to Kanzig (2021) / Kilian-LP responses, scripts/us_passthrough_targets.py; Kanzig 1986-2024 0.061

cyclical_income_elasticity.unit: elasticity to the bloc output gap
cyclical_income_elasticity.source: scaled so that the consumption-weighted mean is 0.85; annual comovement estimate 1.25 (s.e. 0.19), scripts/demand_elasticities.py

crude_share_of_fuel_price_phi.source: US EIA 2025; euro area Fuels Europe/EC Jan 2025 (taxes about half); Japan own arithmetic (taxes about 41%); others judgemental [unverified]

low_demand_elasticity.note: Hamilton (2009) / CCI IV low end of the short-run demand elasticity; same total impact absorption A0, inventories absorb more

high_demand_elasticity.note: Kilian-Murphy (2014) short-run demand elasticity 0.18-0.28; same total impact absorption A0, inventories absorb less

supply_heavy.note: Baumeister-Hamilton / Caldara et al. view: supply 30-45% of price variance (same IRF parameters, larger and more frequent supply shocks, smaller oil-specific innovation)

shale_boom.note: 2009-2019 regime: production elasticity 0.19 at 12 months, 0.28 at 24

shale_discipline.note: 2021-2026 regime: production elasticity 0.06 at 12 months, 0.10 at 24
